recommendations.regimenLabel: Hypertonic saline if severe symptoms; correct slowly by cause
steps: Severe symptoms (seizures, coma): cautious hypertonic 3% saline boluses to raise Na ~4–6 mmol/L.
Correct slowly: ≤8–10 mmol/L per 24 h (avoid osmotic demyelination); recheck Na frequently.
Hypovolaemic: 0.9% saline. SIADH: fluid restriction ± treat cause. Hypervolaemic: treat HF/cirrhosis, restrict fluid.
Identify and remove the cause (drugs, cortisol/thyroid deficiency, malignancy).
Watch for over-correction — re-lower with dextrose/desmopressin if too fast.

drugRefs.dose: 150 mL over 20 min, repeat to raise serum Na by 4–6 mmol/L
drugRefs.freq: repeat boluses to symptom resolution / target rise; recheck Na frequently
drugRefs.why: Rapidly raises sodium to reverse cerebral oedema in severe symptomatic hyponatraemia (seizures/coma); a fluid, not an antibiotic.
Restores volume in hypovolaemic hyponatraemia; not for SIADH (where fluid restriction is used).

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Fluid and Electrolyte Disturbances
European Clinical Practice Guideline on Diagnosis and Treatment of Hyponatraemia
US Expert Panel Recommendations on the Treatment of Hyponatraemia

drugRefs.dose: electrolyte-free water as 5% glucose, titrated to lower Na back to target
drugRefs.why: Free water re-lowers sodium if the 24 h correction limit is exceeded, reducing osmotic demyelination risk.

drugRefs.freq: as needed to control free-water clearance
drugRefs.why: Reintroduces ADH effect to arrest an over-rapid rise in sodium (proactive or reactive strategy).

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Fluid and Electrolyte Disturbances
European Clinical Practice Guideline on Diagnosis and Treatment of Hyponatraemia

decision.label: Correct slowly; 3% saline if severe symptoms; avoid over-correction

confirm: Symptomatic low sodium; assess volume status and serum/urine osmolality to classify (hypovolaemic / euvolaemic-SIADH / hypervolaemic).
